## The learning path

The course has three phases: preparation, one course day, and a follow-up task. The phases are the same in every edition. The [edition pages](editions/hs2026.qmd) give the dates.

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-alt: "Flow chart with three phases. Before the course day: read Bender et al. and describe one generative AI use in your research. On the course day: four analytical lenses in the morning, Panarchy and Ecocycle in the afternoon, then a research-use clinic. After the course day: write a Responsible GenAI Use Statement."
flowchart LR
    A["<b>Before</b><br/>Read Bender et al.<br/>Describe one GenAI use<br/>in your research"] --> B["<b>Course day: morning</b><br/>Four analytical lenses"]
    B --> C["<b>Course day: afternoon</b><br/>Panarchy and Ecocycle<br/>Research-use clinic"]
    C --> D["<b>After</b><br/>Responsible GenAI<br/>Use Statement"]
```

### Before the course day

- Read the required text: Bender et al., _On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots_ [-@bender2021].
- Choose two recommended readings or cases from the [literature](literature.qmd) page.
- Write a short description of one actual or planned use of generative AI in your research. Say why you might use it and what you do not know about it.

The [assignments](assignments.qmd) page gives a proposed plan for the eight hours of preparation.

### On the course day

The morning builds a shared vocabulary. Each lens takes about 35 minutes: a short input, a documented case, and a group activity of 10 to 15 minutes.

1. [Lens 1: Stochastic Parrots — Scale and Environment](lenses/01-scale.qmd). Output: a material-and-provenance map.
2. [Lens 2: Representation and Pygmalion](lenses/02-representation.qmd). Output: a representation and harm pathway.
3. [Lens 3: Lifecycle and Labor](lenses/03-lifecycle-labor.qmd). Output: a lifecycle risk matrix.
4. [Lens 4: Political Economy](lenses/04-political-economy.qmd). Output: a stakeholder and incentive map.

The afternoon applies the vocabulary to the institutions in which participants work.

5. [Panarchy](panarchy.qmd): a facilitated discussion of 130 minutes. Output: a shared chart, three priorities, action owners, and a review point.
6. [Ecocycle](panarchy.qmd#ecocycle-a-30-minute-adaptation): a 30-minute adaptation. Output: a diagnosis of the priority initiatives.
7. Research-use clinic: each participant applies the worksheet to their own research use. Each participant then decides with three questions: constraints, comparison, and accountability. A peer reviews the result.

Your contributions on the day are four lens worksheets, a group Panarchy chart, an Ecocycle diagnosis, and one practical action.

### After the course day

Write a Responsible GenAI Use Statement for your own research. The [assignments](assignments.qmd) page describes the task, the rubric, and the template. The task is a proposal. The instructors and the Graduate Center confirm the binding rules for each edition.
